metadata.note: The original namesake mainline of the whole Pere Marquette system, and a gap in this map's Pere Marquette coverage (previously only a small Sanilac branch and a Detroit-Flint segment, both far from the company's actual core route -- see thumb_michigan_railroads.geojson and detroit_flint.geojson). The Flint and Pere Marquette Railway was incorporated Jan 21 1857 with a federal land grant to build from Flint to 'Pere Marquette' (the settlement at the mouth of the Pere Marquette River, renamed Ludington in 1873/74). Construction began at East Saginaw in 1859; the line reached Clare by 1871, Reed City by Dec 1871 (F&PM was the first railroad into both towns, as it also was at Baldwin), and finally Ludington on Dec 1 1874, completing 170 miles Flint-Ludington (253 route-miles total including the Saginaw branch). Ludington's choice as the western terminus mattered enormously: F&PM launched its first Lake Michigan railroad car ferry (the SS Pere Marquette) in 1896/97, carrying entire loaded freight and passenger cars across the lake to Wisconsin -- eventually three car-ferry routes ran from Ludington to Milwaukee, Manitowoc, and Kewaunee, a business that lasted into the mid-1960s (not modeled here as rail geometry, since the crossing itself was by boat). The Flint and Pere Marquette merged with the Chicago and West Michigan Railway and the Detroit, Grand Rapids and Western Railway in 1900 to form the Pere Marquette Railroad; the Chesapeake and Ohio Railway fully absorbed Pere Marquette in 1947. Geometry is a real-town waypoint approximation (Flint-Saginaw-Clare-Reed City-Baldwin-Ludington), straight-line segments between documented stations -- NOT digitized from period track maps.

metadata.not_yet_sourced: Exact date passenger service ended on this specific Flint-Saginaw-Ludington route (approximated here at Amtrak's May 1 1971 creation, since it was not among the routes Amtrak continued -- not independently confirmed, and plausibly ended earlier given the broader mid-century decline of Michigan branch-line passenger service); precise frequency for any era, all estimated.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
